sources.title: DiDi Global careers job detail (Egypt/Cairo role)
sources.proves: DiDi maintained an Egypt/Cairo organizational hiring footprint; useful as official company evidence, but not a city-by-city live service map.

sources.title: DiDi Rider: Affordable rides
sources.publisher: Apple App Store (Egypt storefront); app by DiDi
sources.proves: The DiDi Rider app is distributed in Egypt's App Store. Storefront availability alone does not prove service in all four Atlas cities.

sources.title: DiDi launches DiDi Express in Cairo, Alexandria
sources.proves: Current secondary evidence of a DiDi product launch in Cairo and Alexandria; supports a Cairo partner story but does not establish Hurghada, El Gouna, Safaga, or Sharm coverage.

sources.title: Prices and schedules: river-bus trips during Eid al-Fitr 2026
sources.proves: A Cairo river-bus leisure service ran daily during Eid 2026 from Happy Land berth at Al-Mazallat to Al-Qanater: EGP 120 per person return, about four hours return sailing, with about three hours at the Qanater berth; also mentions one-hour short trips without an exact published fare.

sources.title: Cairo public transport prepares to receive Maspero river-bus station at Ahl Masr Walk
sources.proves: Maspero was being prepared as a river-bus station and the authority discussed resuming University/Zoo services. This is historical candidate evidence, not proof of operation in July 2026.

sources.title: A ‘Swim Bus’ on the Nile
sources.proves: Egypt's General Authority for River Transport described a trial amphibious tourist bus for Cairo. The article explicitly says tourism only, not public passenger transport; this must remain future/opportunity evidence rather than a live corridor.

sources.title: AD Ports Group Launches Cruise and Ferry Terminal Services in Egypt, Strengthening Cruise Tourism Across the Red Sea
sources.proves: Cruise services commenced at Sharm El Sheikh, Hurghada, and Safaga terminals; passenger services launched at Hurghada and Safaga; Safaga–NEOM ferry operations supported Hajj-worker transport. No passenger volume or public fare is stated.

sources.title: AD Ports Group and Red Sea Port Authority Sign Three Concession Agreements to Strengthen Egypt’s Cruise Tourism Sector at Safaga, Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh Ports
sources.proves: Official concession evidence naming the three real cruise terminals and a 15-year operating/development arrangement with Egypt's Red Sea Ports Authority; in 2024 they were expected operational in 2025, superseded by S7's May 2026 commencement evidence.

sources.title: Island Life
sources.publisher: Experience Egypt, Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.proves: Giftun Islands are a short boat ride from Hurghada, visits are pre-arranged and fee-bearing, and special Mahmeya boats run daily from Hurghada each morning and return at sunset. Exact departure berth, fare, capacity, and annual riders are not supplied.

sources.title: Sharm al-Sheikh
sources.publisher: Experience Egypt, Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.proves: Official tourism framing for Sharm as a major marine resort between Ras Muhammad National Park and Nabq Protectorate, with an international airport. It supports destination context, not a currently scheduled water route or berth.

sources.title: Boat Rentals
sources.proves: El Gouna officially markets boat rentals and water-based leisure from its resort environment. The page does not identify a public passenger terminal, scheduled corridor, route fare, or passenger count.

sources.title: Egypt tourism records historic growth in 2025 receiving 19 million tourists
sources.publisher: Egypt State Information Service, citing Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.proves: Egypt received nearly 19 million tourists in 2025, 21% above 2024. This is a national tourism context metric and must not be converted into route demand.

sources.title: Cairo Int'l Airport records 2025 daily traffic peak with 103,000 passengers
sources.publisher: Egypt State Information Service, citing Ministry of Civil Aviation
sources.proves: Cairo International Airport handled 30.94 million passengers in 2025 (up 6.8% from 28.97 million in 2024) and a 103,000-passenger daily peak. Airport throughput is not Nile-route demand.

sources.title: Egypt Partners with IFC to Introduce Public Private Partnerships at 11 Airports
sources.publisher: International Finance Corporation with Government of Egypt
sources.proves: Hurghada International Airport was selected as the PPP pilot and described as Egypt's second busiest by annual passengers and aviation traffic. No exact passenger total is provided on the page.

demand_records.assumption_record: National arrivals are context only. No allocation to Cairo, Hurghada, Sharm, any terminal, or any water corridor is permitted without a sourced segmentation model.
Airport throughput includes arrivals, departures, connections, and potentially repeated persons. It is not converted to Nile route demand.
Peak-day throughput is a seasonality/operations marker only and is not annualized or converted to transfer demand.

brief_maturity.recommendation: Enhance, do not replace, the canonical briefs once available. The immediate editorial win is a visibly separate Cairo/Nile story and Red Sea gateway/island story, with a strict current-service versus opportunity label.

partner_narrative_notes.placement: partner-specific block only; do not copy DiDi claims into canonical city/cluster briefs
Cairo_Nile: Position DiDi as the land-side digital connective tissue to verified Nile departure points, beginning with a station-level pilot rather than claiming a citywide water network.
Use Cairo International Airport's 30.94 million 2025 passenger throughput only as transfer context; do not imply a conversion rate to Nile rides.
The defensible proof point is the EGP 120 Happy Land–Al-Qanater return Eid service. Maspero and University/Zoo stations remain revalidation leads.
Exclude the trial amphibious bus from live public-transit claims because the cited authority description says tourist-only and trial basis.
Red_Sea: Lead with three now-operating cruise terminals—Hurghada, Safaga, Sharm—and a clear first/last-mile handoff proposition around passenger gates, hotels, airports, and resorts.
Use Hurghada–Mahmeya/Giftun as evidence that fee-bearing daily boat demand exists, while explicitly stating that the departure berth, fare, and annual volume remain unverified.
Treat Safaga–NEOM as a real, seasonal/special-purpose international ferry flow, not as a mass-market commuter route.
Treat Ras Muhammad, Nabq, and El Gouna water activity as future adjacencies until a named authorized terminal and current operator schedule are sourced.
partner_narrative_notes.DiDi_current_evidence_boundary: Cairo is supported by a 2025 product-launch report plus official Egypt/Cairo organizational evidence. This research does not prove live DiDi service in Hurghada, El Gouna, Safaga, or Sharm; proposals should say coverage validation required.
partner_narrative_notes.finance_handoff: No Egypt route is finance-ready. Keep annual_one_way_pax null. The sole current route fare captured is EGP 120 return for a specific Eid 2026 Cairo leisure service.
